articles.headline: How to bet Falcons-Packers on TNF: Analysis, tips and top plays
articles.description: Odds, bets and analysis to help you bet Falcons-Packers on "Thursday Night Football."
articles.body:
"Thursday Night Football" features the Atlanta Falcons visiting Lambeau Field to take on the Green Bay Packers. With Michael Penix Jr. healthy and slated to start, the Falcons get some stability at the quarterback position. Off to an 0-2 start, behind an offense that couldn't find any sense of rhythm with No. 3 QB Cooper Rush taking snaps, we finally get to see how coach Kevin Stefanski schemes for his two playmakers in the pass game -- Drake London and Kyle Pitts Sr. -- versus a Packers defense that is playing zone coverage on 70.5% of opponent dropbacks.

Now, Stefanski's call sheet will be based off the volume for running back Bijan Robinson, who is averaging 18.5 carries per game. We should see a lot of outside zone schemes (which should mirror the play-action passing game) versus a Green Bay defense allowing only 2.9 YPC (second fewest in the league) through the first two weeks.

For the Packers, quarterback Jordan Love has completed only 52.1% of his passes to start the season, but he has hit on eight explosive-play throws (20 or more yards), which ranks fifth in the league. Christian Watson is a big-play target who has scored three touchdowns through two weeks, while Matthew Golden is emerging as a go-to option. It's a committee approach in the backfield, one that lacks difference-making ability.

Betting outlook

Looking at a line that has dropped to Green Bay -4.5, I'm going to take the Packers to cover the spread (and a moneyline bet), plus I'm hitting the over at 42.5. I like Love and the Green Bay pass game against a Falcons defense that struggled in Week 2 versus the Panthers and quarterback Bryce Young (287 yards, three touchdowns). Expect more rhythm throws to the middle of the field, plus the isolation shots to Watson. And I think Green Bay can get enough out of this makeshift backfield (Kaleb Johnson flashed on tape last week) to sustain and control tempo. Plus, I'm betting on that Packers defense to win enough early-down situations to keep the Falcons' offense off schedule based on the game plan. We know Robinson will get his touches, and there will be schemed throws for Penix to hit based on Stefanski's history as a playcaller. But I don't think it's enough to cover or knock off the Packers at the home opener at Lambeau Field.

Total points UNDER 42.5 (-108)

Ben Solak: The Falcons finally get functional quarterback play with Penix healthy and stepping in, but he was not even an average starter when we last saw him and now takes snaps in a new offense and having seen no preseason action. I'm expecting plenty of rust against a solid Packers defense. On the other side of the ball, DC Jeff Ulbrich remains a quality designer of pressure packages -- something with which the Packers' young and injury-riddled O-line is likely to struggle. I see sacks, punts and field goals in this one.

articles.headline: Why Patriots must be better at managing the clock before halftime
articles.description: After two straight games with questionable decisions before halftime, the Patriots admit they need to improve on possessions late in the second quarter.
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel and quarterback Drake Maye are working to regain their edge in an area they mastered last season but have fallen short in the first two games of the 2026 season.

Can they reclaim their standing among the NFL's best in the possession directly before halftime?

Back-to-back road games against 2025 AFC playoff teams in the Jacksonville Jaguars (1-1) and Buffalo Bills (2-0) provide a tough test to get back on track when points will be at a premium. The Jaguars have scored 43 points through two games and the Bills have scored 77. 

"I felt like it was one of the best things that we did last year -- whether getting points or ending with the football," Maye said Wednesday after the team's first practice in preparation for Sunday's contest against the Jaguars (1 p.m. ET, CBS). "When the defense gives you the ball back, you try to end with the football in the first half, especially when we're coming out and having the ball in the second half. That's definitely a big emphasis for us."

A combination of game-management hiccups by Vrabel and VP of game strategy and operations John Streicher and Maye's decision-making has contributed to a disappointing start in 2026.

Maye and the offense had the ball on their own 20 with 1:48 on the clock in last Sunday's 20-3 win over the Steelers. They led 10-0 and still had all three of their timeouts. But the drive never got started, with Maye running into a sack on a three-man rush on first down.

"That's definitely something you have to know the time and place, speaking for myself, of getting the ball forward, [even] an incomplete pass and it's second-and-10," Maye said. "When you're under two minutes and you let them get three [points] from it, that's one of our jobs on offense [to not let that happen]."

The Patriots (1-1) punted back to the Steelers (1-1), who took over at their own 35-yard line with 40 seconds left. Vrabel gifted the Steelers an additional 5 yards with 12 seconds remaining when he called timeout and was penalized for delay of game. On the prior play, cornerback Marcus Jones was injured and the Patriots were assessed a timeout as a result, per league rules when there is less than two minutes on the clock, which meant they couldn't call timeout again before the next snap.

"I blew it," Vrabel acknowledged, explaining that he had been talking with officials on why Steelers tight end Pat Freiermuth was ruled to be out of bounds when his shin appeared to come down in the field of play. "I was all caught up on the fact that they should've been winding [the clock on] that play, which again, I don't understand."

The Steelers capitalized with a 56-yard field goal on the final play of the half.

articles.headline: Marc Curella 'sent a subtle message' to try to tempt Rodri into Real Madrid move
articles.description: Real Madrid's Marc Cucurella has said he "sent a subtle message" asking Rodri to join him at Real Madrid this summer, before the midfielder opted to sign for rivals Barcelona.
articles.body:
Real Madrid's Marc Cucurella has said he "sent a subtle message" asking Rodri to join him at Real Madrid this summer, before the midfielder opted to sign for rivals Barcelona.

Madrid were close to landing Rodri from Manchester City as part of their major rebuild ahead of this season, but Spain's World Cup-winning captain chose to move to Barça instead -- with Hansi Flick's side now six points clear at the top of the LaLiga table.

Both players are now with the Spain squad preparing for Saturday's Nations League game against England and Wembley, and -- speaking to Cadena SER radio -- Cucurella admitted he'd made it clear to Rodri that he'd like to have him as a teammate at the Bernabéu.

"I don't really like pressuring or influencing teammates," Cucurella said. "These are personal things. It's true that I sent him a subtle message, before the news broke, saying I hoped we'd become teammates.

"He replied, but didn't give anything away. I'm happy for him [at Barça], though I hope he doesn't have too much success."

Cucurella was one of six new signings at Madrid, joining new coach José Mourinho, but the team are facing criticism after suffering two losses already, at Real Betis and in last weekend's derby with Atlético Madrid.

"We didn't finish the period before the break in the best way," Cucurella said. "It's all a process, but the important thing is to build a solid foundation... Let's see if we can find a good balance and build a strong, united group. If the season ends the way we all want it to, no one will remember the start."

Atletico targeted Madrid's left-flank, made up of Cucurella and Vinícius Júnior, repeatedly in the derby.

- Barcelona follow Real Madrid in breaking €1 billion revenue barrier

- Real Madrid conspiracy claims dismissed as a 'smokescreen' by LaLiga president

- Lamine Yamal rejects goal stats for Ballon d'Or for 'players that make you dream'

"It's good playing with Vini, but ultimately, we've barely had any training time," Cucurella said. "Connecting with me is different compared to other full-backs, but it's a process. From what I see, and with the effort he's putting in -- knowing it's not his natural strength -- Vinicius is really doing his part."

Statistics show Madrid's players cover less total distance than their LaLiga rivals so far this season, but Cucurella denied that that's a problem.

"That stat surprised me," he said. "But we do run a lot. We're talking about these figures because we lost the derby against Atleti. If we hadn't lost, no one would be mentioning it."

articles.headline: Ranking eight winless NFL teams: Texans, Bucs, others at 0-2
articles.description: Can the Texans turn it around (again)? Do the Buccaneers, Colts or Chargers have a chance to get right? Is the season already over for the Falcons and Dolphins?
articles.body:
This time every year, I tell you that the NFL playoffs secretly start in Week 3. For the league's 0-2 teams, Week 3 might as well be an eliminator game.

In an era with 17 games and 14 playoff teams, it's possible to dig out of an 0-2 hole and make it to the postseason, something three teams managed to do in 2025. Two of them -- the Bears and Panthers -- even managed to win their divisions at the end of the year.

But since 2002, 102 teams have started their seasons by losing three consecutive games. Even if we expand our scope and treat the seventh seed from 2002 to 2019 as a would-be playoff team, just four of those 102 teams overcame their 0-3 start and finished in the playoff picture, for an advancement rate of 3.9%. Two of them were Mike Tomlin-led Steelers teams that finished seventh in the AFC in 2013 and 2019, missing the postseason because the league hadn't yet gone to the 14-team field.

The other two teams were both editions of the Texans -- and they actually did advance to the playoffs. One came in 2018. The other was last season's Houston squad. The Texans started 0-3, losing to the Rams, Buccaneers and Jaguars by a combined 13 points. From that point forward, they went 12-2, with their only losses coming to the eventual top seeds in the AFC (Broncos) and NFC (Seahawks).

Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show'

Here we are one year later, and the Texans are back again, joining seven other winless teams through two weeks of the 2026 season. They'll be in the only matchup of 0-2 teams in Week 3 as they travel to Indianapolis to play the Colts. Can they get back on track and avoid needing to defy history yet again? Are there any other teams that have a shot at making it back from 0-2 to advance into the playoffs?

Today, I'll take stock of the eight 0-2 teams around the NFL, break down why each has gotten off to a slow start and rank their chances of still sneaking into the postseason. I also included chances to make the playoffs via ESPN's Football Power Index.

For teams such as the Dolphins, a playoff berth in 2026 wasn't really in the cards to begin with. For many of the teams ahead of Miami, though, there's going to be a sense of urgency to fix things quickly. Nobody wants to give up on their playoff dreams and start thinking about 2027 after three weeks. The Falcons have the first chance to get into the win column with a Thursday night matchup against Green Bay, but they aren't No. 1 on this list as the most likely 0-2 team to turn it around.

Jump to an 0-2 team:

MIA | TB | TEN | WSH

Chances of advancing to the postseason, via ESPN's FPI: 41.8% (16th highest)

Well, as we just discussed, the Texans have been here before, starting 0-3 and living to tell the tale in January -- even after losing quarterback C.J. Stroud for a month. articles.headline: Ben Rice tops Aaron Boone's preseason prediction, passes 40 HRs
articles.description: Yankees manager Aaron Boone predicted during spring training that Ben Rice would finish with 39 home runs this season. Rice is two-up after hitting Nos. 40 and 41 in a 9-2 victory over the Rays, tying for the AL home run lead.
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- Ben Rice one-upped Aaron Boone. And then he two-upped the Yankees manager.

Boone predicted during spring training that Rice would finish with 39 home runs this season. Rice hit Nos. 40 and 41 in Wednesday night's 9-2 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays, tying for the American League home run lead.

He smiled and pointed at Boone when he returned to the dugout after driving Mason Englert's first pitch of the game into Yankee Stadium's right-field second deck. Rice grinned at Boone some more after another solo homer in the fourth.

"I think I said, 'Hey, there's 40 for you,'" Rice recalled. "I was joking with him after the 41st one, saying, 'Hey, thanks for inspiring me this year.' But it's all in good fun. Back in spring when he told me that, I knew that secretly meant he was hoping I'd hit 40."

Rice is tied for the AL home run lead with Baltimore's Pete Alonso, Tampa Bay's Junior Caminero and Houston's Yordan Alvarez. He is hitting .263 and leads the Yankees with 97 RBIs and a .900 OPS, becoming a first-time All-Star and the biggest cog in an offense missing Aaron Judge and Giancarlo Stanton for most of the season.

Boone deliberately picked an odd total rather than a round figure.

"I was confident he was going to have a really big year," he said. "Probably wanted to make sure it was just south of a number, maybe to maybe let him know that."

Rice, who had three hits and a walk, became the 13th Yankees player with a 40-home run season but just the third to reach the milestone during his first three seasons after Joe DiMaggio and Judge. Rice's plate appearances often prompt a rendition of Elton John's "Bennie and the Jets″ from the stadium's organist, and Rice has sparked an often struggling offense with 16 go-ahead homers this year and three that have tied games.

"One thing I always tell guys, the difference between minor leaguers and big leaguers is the consistency," Judge said. "He's one of the best. I can look up at the clock and I know exactly where he's going to be in the cage. you know what he's doing in the training room, the weight room. It's just every single day, man. This guy's a machine."

A 12th-round pick in the 2021 amateur draft from Dartmouth, where he played just 30 games over three years due to the coronavirus pandemic, Rice was mostly a catcher but occasionally a first baseman in the minors. He made his big league debut in June 2024 at age 25 after Anthony Rizzo broke a forearm.

Rice hit .171 with seven homers and 23 RBIs in 50 games that year then batted .255 with 26 homers and 65 RBIs in 138 games last year.

With Stanton sidelined for most of the season, the left-handed-hitting Rice has 93 games at designated hitter this year and 52 at first.

"It's tough to pull him off his back leg," Yankees pitcher Gerrit Cole said. "He's really able to stay balanced and deliver high-efficacy strikes on various pitches in all parts of the zone."

articles.headline: With Kyler Murray back, will Vikings open up passing attack?
articles.description: Coach Kevin O'Connell said he is "still a believer in explosives" despite a long stretch of tepid air production for Minnesota.
articles.body:
EAGAN, Minn. -- Inside the visitors locker room Sunday at Soldier Field, Minnesota Vikings players peeled off layers of rain-soaked uniforms and equipment. Coach Kevin O'Connell soon launched into a postgame speech that precisely depicted his mindset, excitement -- and maybe even a bit of distress after a 9-3 victory over the Chicago Bears.

O'Connell praised players for "trying to figure out a way to find a way."

Later, he roared: "The only thing that matters is winning!"

That line represented the culmination of a very public reckoning O'Connell has put himself through while heading into his fifth season in Minnesota. The Vikings (2-0) have won seven consecutive games, dating back to last season, in ways that are almost unrecognizable from the pass-happy teams he first fielded upon arrival in 2022. But as quarterback Kyler Murray returns to the field, and with a hot but otherwise clear weather forecast Sunday at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (4:05 p.m. ET, Fox), O'Connell has far from given up on the passing game he craves. 

"I'm still a believer in explosives," he said Monday. "I'm still a believer in taking some yards when they present themselves and doing it at a level where we pitch and catch at a level that I know our guys are capable of."

From 2022 to 2024, the Vikings put up the NFL's third-most passing yards (12,886) with the league's fifth-lowest rate of designed running plays (35.3%). They built their offense around receiver Justin Jefferson, who averaged a league-best 100.4 receiving yards per game over that period. Since that point, however, the Vikings rank No. 31 in passing yards (3,093) and have the league's fifth-fewest number of offensive plays -- rushing or passing -- that have gone for 10 yards or more (197). They've had fewer than 200 passing yards in 16 of their past 21 games.

Fortunately for them, that stretch has coincided with a defense and special teams that have been among the NFL's best, ranking No. 3 and 7 in expected points added (EPA), respectively. 

During their unbeaten start this season, with Murray playing only 11 snaps because of a concussion and leading rusher Jordan Mason going on injured reserve with a thumb injury after one week, the Vikings have managed a league-low 13 plays of 10 or more yards. O'Connell has protected the offense, particularly last week in Chicago, by leaning on the run game more than all but one other NFL playcaller. His rate of designed runs (50%) is higher than every team but the Seattle Seahawks, who also lost their starting quarterback (Sam Darnold) early in Week 1. Relatedly, the Vikings are tied with the Seahawks and Cincinnati Bengals for the NFL's fewest turnovers this season (one). 

"You've got to learn some things on how you approach trying to win one game every Sunday," O'Connell said this summer. "And they're all different. Every weekend is a challenge schematically, personnel-wise, where your team's at from a health standpoint, where your team's at with certain positions.

articles.headline: Denver Broncos to face another MVP QB in Matthew Stafford
articles.description: Sunday marks the 10th time the Broncos have faced an MVP quarterback since Vance Joseph became defensive coordinator in 2023. Can Denver get the best of Stafford?
articles.body:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- In weeks when the Denver Broncos are pitted against one of the NFL's best quarterbacks, defensive coordinator Vance Joseph often responds with a sigh when asked questions about how to stop them.

"That's our league, you know?" Joseph said. "Every week, every season, every time I look up I kind of feel like there is a quarterback waiting who can just punish you. Every week, man."

This is one of those weeks, as the Broncos will host the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday night at Empower Field at Mile High (8:20 p.m. ET, NBC). Reigning MVP Matthew Stafford will stand across from Joseph's defense six days after his 69th career 300-yard passing game and his 22nd career game with at least four touchdown passes.

He is also the last remaining active player who has been an NFL MVP that Joseph will face since being hired as Denver's defensive coordinator in 2023. The Broncos have played against Patrick Mahomes, Lamar Jackson, Aaron Rodgers and Josh Allen at least once since, and Sunday's match-up against Stafford and the Rams will complete the set.

The five quarterbacks have won a combined 10 MVP awards, including the last eight. They've had 10 meetings (including playoffs) against the Broncos over the past three-plus seasons. Denver has already faced one former MVP this season, losing to Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs 31-10 in the season opener. The loss to Mahomes makes those former MVPs 5-5 against the Broncos since Joseph became defensive coordinator.

The Broncos have allowed one 300-yard passing game in that stretch -- Mahomes threw for 306 yards in Week 6 of the 2023 season. They have thrown a combined 14 touchdown passes to nine interceptions and have been sacked 27 times (2.7 per game). Jackson had the best all-around day from that batch, completing 16 of 19 passes for 280 yards and three touchdowns in the Ravens' 41-10 win over the Broncos in Week 9 of the 2024 season. Allen had 283 passing yards and three touchdowns with two interceptions in the Broncos' overtime divisional round win this past January.

"Every week is a tough week because everybody has players who can make plays," Broncos cornerback Pat Surtain II said. "... But those quarterbacks at the top of their games, they force you to pay attention to all the details because the smallest things, the little details, that's all they need to put you in a bad spot. And once they find a bad spot, they're not going away from it until you take care of it."

The Broncos' defense re-calibrated from their Week 1 loss to the Chiefs with a Week 2 win over Jacksonville. The Broncos improved from giving up 173 rushing yards to Kenneth Walker III and missing an alarming 19 tackles against Kansas City to allow only 115 net yards and three points to the Jaguars in the second half to spark a comeback win. The Jaguars had 64 combined yards in their final three possessions of the game, which included an interception by Broncos cornerback Riley Moss.

articles.description: Bayern Munich attacking midfielder Lennart Karl could get his dream move to Real Madrid. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich attacking midfielder Lennart Karl could get his dream move to Real Madrid, while AC Milan are planning to sign USMNT winger Christian Pulisic to a new contract. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Real Madrid are keeping tabs on Bayern Munich attacking midfielder Lennart Karl, according to Bild's Christian Falk. Los Blancos are among several teams interested in the 18-year-old, with whom the Bundesliga champions plan to open contract renewal talks, while rival clubs monitor whether Michael Olise's presence in his position could create a transfer opportunity. Karl said during an event in January that playing for Madrid would be a "dream" which led to an apology after the comments sparked anger among Bayern fans.

- AC Milan are planning to sign USMNT winger Christian Pulisic to a new contract extending until the summer of 2031, according to Corriere dello Sport. Initial talks have begun with the 28-year-old's representatives over a deal worth around €5 million per season following his goal-scoring performance in Sunday's 3-0 win over Lecce.

- Chelsea are considering Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton and Feyenoord's Gjivai Zechiël as potential successors to Enzo Fernández, TEAMtalk reports. The 22-year-old Zechiel has registered five goals and four assists in seven Eredivisie matches this season, attracting interest from Chelsea, Liverpool, and five other Premier League clubs.

- Manchester City left back Rayan Aït-Nouri is being scouted by Juventus, according to Gazzetta dello Sport. The 25-year-old tops the Bianconeri shortlist for the January transfer window, with a loan approach lined up due to his lack of playing time under Enzo Maresca, while RB Leipzig's David Raum is considered an alternative.

- Tottenham Hotspur and Aston Villa are interested in Bayern Munich defender Kim Min-Jae, according to Christian Falk. Both clubs have tracked the 29-year-old South Korea international since the summer, though any move is expected to depend on upcoming contract discussions with the German club.
